([[Huntersville, North Carolina]]) | college = [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] (2024–2026) | draft_year = | draft_round = | draft_pick = | draft_team = | career_start = | years1 = | team1 = | highlights = * Third-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] (2026) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2024 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2024]]) * 2× [[North Carolina Mr. Basketball]] (2023, 2024) }} '''Isaiah Demonte Evans''' (born December 6, 2005) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. ==Early life and high school== Evans grew up in [[Charlotte, North Carolina]] and attended [[North Mecklenburg High School]] in [[Huntersville, North Carolina]].{{cite web|url=https://www.wcnc.com/article/sports/north-mecks-isaiah-evans-one-of-top-juniors-in-the-nation/275-918a6762-2669-4f9d-8c45-63ffb8f1dca5|title=North Meck's Isaiah Evans one of top juniors in the nation|first=Nick|last=Carboni|website=[[WCNC-TV|WCNC.com]]|date=January 13, 2023|access-date=January 31, 2024}} He averaged 26 points and 6.4 rebounds per game as a junior.{{cite web|url=https://www.wbtv.com/2023/11/13/isaiah-evans-signs-with-duke/|title=North Meck star Isaiah Evans signs with Duke|first=Nate|last=Wimberly|website=[[WBTV|WBTV.com]]|date=November 13, 2023|access-date=February 27, 2024}} Evans averaged 38.6 points over five games in the [[North Carolina High School Athletic Association|NCHSAA]] 4A state playoffs and was named [[North Carolina Mr. Basketball]] at the end of the season.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/nevada/Article/duke-hosting-five-star-isaiah-evans-for-an-official-visit-this-weekend-208327694/?Page=6|title=Duke hosting Five-Star Isaiah Evans for an official visit this weekend|first=Adam|last=Lowe|website=[[247Sports.com]]|date=April 14, 2023|access-date=February 27, 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/high-school/article274812646.html|title=Duke men's basketball gets commitment from top high school player in North Carolina|first=Langston|last=Wertz Jr.|work=[[The Charlotte Observer]]|date=April 27, 2023|access-date=February 28, 2024}} Evans averaged 27.4 points, 6.1 rebounds, 3.2 assists and 2.3 steals per contest to guide the Vikings to a 30–3 record and a NCHSAA 4A state championship. He was selected to play in the [[2024 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] during his senior year.{{cite web|url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/high-school/article284596915.html|title=North Meck's Isaiah Evans among 5 NC players named to 2024 McDonald's All-American games|first=Langston|last=Wertz Jr.|work=[[The Charlotte Observer]]|date=January 23, 2024|access-date=January 31, 2024}} Evans also repeated as North Carolina Mr. Basketball.{{cite web|url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/high-school/article286480080.html|title=North Mecklenburg standout Isaiah Evans is NC Mr. Basketball for second straight year|work=[[The Charlotte Observer]]|date=March 14, 2024|access-date=March 17, 2024}} He was also named the Gatorade North Carolina Player of the Year for boys basketball.{{Cite web |title=Gatorade 2023 - 2024: Player of the Year Boys Basketball - North Carolina |url=https://playeroftheyear.gatorade.com/winner/isaiah-evans/40242 |website=Gatorade Player of the Year}} ===Recruiting=== Evans was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2024 class, according to major recruiting services.{{cite web|url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/high-school/article281437528.html|title=Get to know five-star Duke recruit Isaiah Evans|work=[[The Charlotte Observer]]|date=November 13, 2023|access-date=February 27, 2024}}{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/duke/recruiting/duke-basketball-baby-ingram-erupts-rival-2-24|title=Five-Star Duke Basketball Signee 'Baby Ingram' Erupts Against Rival|first=Matt|last=Giles|website=[[SI.com]]|date=February 3, 2024|access-date=February 28, 2024}} He committed to play [[college basketball]] at [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] over offers from [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]], [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]], [[Tennessee Volunteers basketball|Tennessee]], [[Texas Longhorns men's basketball|Texas]], [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], and [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]].{{cite web|url=https://www.fayobserver.com/story/sports/college/acc/2023/04/27/isaiah-evans-duke-basketball-commit-darren-harris-class-of-2024/70161612007/|title=Duke basketball lands five-star in-state recruit Isaiah Evans|first=Monica|last=Holland|work=[[The Fayetteville Observer]]|date=April 27, 2023|access-date=February 27, 2024}} Evans signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play for the Blue Devils on November 13, 2023, during the early signing period.{{cite web|url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/high-school/article281780168.html|title=Duke Blue Devils basketball recruit Isaiah Evans signs NLI|work=[[The Charlotte Observer]]|date=November 13, 2023|access-date=January 31, 2024}} == College career == Evans enrolled at [[Duke University]] in June 2024 in order to take part in the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Blue Devils]]' summer practices.{{cite web |date=June 22, 2024 |title=Duke basketball observations from Blue Devils' summer scrimmage ahead of 2024-25 season |url=https://www.fayobserver.com/story/sports/college/acc/2024/06/22/duke-basketball-scrimmage-jon-scheyer-cooper-flagg-caleb-foster-tyrese-proctor-sion-james/74174519007/ |access-date=September 30, 2024 |work=[[The Fayetteville Observer]]}} Evans spent his freshman season playing behind future first-overall draft pick [[Cooper Flagg]] and averaged 6.8 points, 1.1 rebounds, and 0.5 assists per game.{{Cite web |title=Isaiah Evans - 2025-26 - Men's Basketball |url=https://goduke.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/isaiah-evans/23104 |access-date=February 23, 2026 |website=Duke University |language=en}} After the season he initially declared for the [[2025 NBA draft]], but ultimately decided to return to Duke for his sophomore season.{{Cite web |last=Baxley |first=Rodd |title=Jon Scheyer's conversations with Isaiah Evans about NBA Draft, coming back to Duke basketball |url=https://www.fayobserver.com/story/sports/college/acc/2025/07/16/duke-basketball-isaiah-evans-stats-jon-scheyer-nba-draft/84594032007/ |access-date=February 23, 2026 |website=The Fayetteville
